definitions.explanation: the characteristic scenery of winter — bare trees, snow, cold skies, and a stark atmosphere

examples.japanese: {窓|まど}から{冬景色|ふゆげしき}を{眺|なが}める。
examples.english: I gaze at the winter scenery from the window.

examples.japanese: {雪|ゆき}に{覆|おお}われた{冬景色|ふゆげしき}が{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: The snow-covered winter landscape is beautiful.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}の{車窓|しゃそう}から{見|み}える{冬景色|ふゆげしき}は、{夏|なつ}とはまるで{違|ちが}う{趣|おもむき}がある。
examples.english: The winter scenery seen from the train window has a completely different charm from summer.

notes:
A compound noun combining {冬|ふゆ} (winter) with {景色|けしき} (scenery). The initial k of {景色|けしき} voices to g (rendaku) in this compound. Evokes a poetic, aesthetic appreciation of winter's sparse beauty.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冬景色|ふゆげしき}が{広|ひろ}がる: winter scenery spreads out
- {一面|いちめん}の{冬景色|ふゆげしき}: winter scenery as far as the eye can see
- {冬景色|ふゆげしき}を{楽|たの}しむ: to enjoy winter scenery

RELATED SEASONAL COMPOUNDS:
- {春景色|はるげしき}: spring landscape
- {夏景色|なつげしき}: summer landscape
- {秋景色|あきげしき}: autumn landscape

CULTURAL NOTE:
{冬景色|ふゆげしき} is also the title of a famous Japanese song ({唱歌|しょうか}) taught in schools, celebrating the quiet beauty of a winter morning. The word carries literary and nostalgic associations beyond its literal meaning.
